extra_misconceptions.fact: Dull blades require excessive force and slip off wood fibers unpredictably, causing deeper lacerations than sharp tools.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A dull carving knife is safer for beginners because the rounded edge cannot slice skin easily.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pulling against the entry angle breaks the wood fibers beneath the skin; always withdraw splinters along their entry path.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling a deep wood splinter out against the entry angle extracts the fragment faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hydrogen peroxide damages healthy healing tissue; flush minor cuts with clean running water and mild soap before bandaging.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hydrogen peroxide should be poured into every fresh carving cut to sterilize the wound.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lifting a dressing disrupts forming clots and restarts bleeding; press fresh gauze directly on top of the soaked pad.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Peeking under a blood-soaked gauze pad every minute verifies whether bleeding has stopped.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Blade locks can fail under sideways twisting or prying forces, so pressure must always keep the blade opening against the stop.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A locking pocketknife makes it safe to push or pry with the spine and tip of the blade.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fixed blades should be sheathed before passing, or handed handle-first with the dull spine toward the receiver until acknowledged.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passing an open fixed-blade carving knife handle-first with the edge facing down is enough.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A cut-resistant thumb guard belongs on the holding hand, while the carving hand needs direct grip sensitivity on the handle.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing a heavy leather glove on the knife-holding hand prevents accidental blade slips.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Loose blades strike each other and nick their cutting edges; each gouge requires an individual edge guard or separate pocket.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Setting unsheathed gouges loose in a tool roll protects their bevels between carving sessions.

extra_socratic_questions: What distance around a carver defines a clear safety circle before opening a pocketknife?
Which spoken confirmation signals that a recipient has a firm grip during a tool handoff?
Under what condition does a non-locking folding knife fold onto the carver's fingers?
Why is it dangerous to rest a workpiece directly on your thigh while roughing out a blank?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Steep bevel angles wedge and tear wood fibers instead of slicing cleanly; carving knives require a fifteen to twenty degree bevel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sharpening a carving knife at a steep forty-five-degree angle creates a better slicing edge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A leather strop only polishes and maintains an existing sharp edge; nicked or rounded blades must be reshaped on a stone first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stropping on leather replaces stone honing even when a blade has visible edge nicks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Oil clogs the pores of a waterstone and ruins its abrasive action; lubricate waterstones exclusively with clean water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying light machine oil to a Japanese waterstone improves metal removal during honing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-speed dry grinding quickly overheats thin steel and ruins its temper; hand stones and strops preserve blade hardness.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using a high-speed bench grinder is the best way to touch up thin carving knife blades.

extra_socratic_questions: Which sharpening stone profile matches the inside curvature of a U-gouge or V-parting tool?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A paring cut uses finger squeezing motion while the thumb braces firmly against the wood to prevent the blade from striking the body.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A paring cut is powered by pulling the entire arm backward toward the carver's chest.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Prying snaps the delicate knife tip and tears wood fibers; slice deeper along both angled walls until the chip releases freely.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Prying out a stuck V-cut chip with the knife tip leaves a clean, crisp groove bottom.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Deep single cuts wedge the blade and split the grain ahead of the edge, whereas shallow passes maintain full directional control.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Making a single deep pass removes waste wood more cleanly than several shallow cuts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Establish the vertical stop cut first so that subsequent slicing cuts terminate cleanly against severed wood fibers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Slicing into a corner before making a vertical stop cut prevents the wood from splitting.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should the thumb of your carving hand anchor during a controlled paring cut?
What happens to wood grain beyond a boundary line if you omit the initial stop cut?
Why does anchoring your opposite thumb on the blade spine limit travel in a push cut?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Balsa crushes under the knife edge instead of slicing cleanly; fine-grained basswood or butternut holds crisp carved details.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Balsa wood is the ideal timber for detailed chip carving because it is the softest wood.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Yellow pine has alternating bands of soft springwood and rock-hard summerwood that deflect blades and cause sudden slips.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Construction-grade yellow pine boards carve smoothly because softwoods are always soft.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unseasoned green wood shrinks unevenly as moisture escapes, causing finished relief plaques to warp and split radially.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Freshly cut green tree branches can be carved into finished plaques without cracking.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cutting against rising grain lifts and splits wood fibers deep into the project, so every cut must follow the downhill grain.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wood grain direction only matters during final sanding rather than during roughing cuts.

extra_socratic_questions: Which grain property makes basswood easier to carve cleanly than red oak or southern pine?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Working all sides progressively at the same stage preserves reference planes and keeps proportions balanced around the centerline.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carving one side of a three-dimensional figure to completion first guarantees symmetry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sandpaper embeds microscopic abrasive grit into wood fibers that rapidly dulls sharp knife edges on subsequent carving cuts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sanding the wood blank between knife passes makes the remaining carving cuts smoother.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Short grain snaps easily across narrow features like legs or bills; orient the longest and thinnest parts parallel to the grain.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Aligning the thinnest appendages of a figure across the short grain adds structural strength.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Early detail work gets accidentally sliced off during roughing; establish major planes and proportions before adding fine textures.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carving fine facial details before roughing out the overall block saves time on a figure.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ballpoint ink soaks deep into wood pores and bleeds under clear finishes; use light pencil or graphite transfer paper instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Transferring a chip carving pattern with heavy ballpoint pen ink washes off after carving.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Low-relief carving creates strong depth in shallow wood by leveling the background and slightly undercutting the subject edges.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Relief carving requires a thick timber block to make the foreground subject stand out.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Chip carving knives slice at a consistent fifty-five to sixty-five degree angle so all three cuts meet at a single bottom point.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Chip carving uses a vertical ninety-degree blade angle to excavate triangular recesses.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unsupported plaques vibrate and snap under gouge pressure; support the entire back flat against a bench hook or non-slip mat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clamping a thin relief plaque strictly by one corner gives full access without flexing.
